strengths: Novel application of information-theoretic concepts to characterize semantic emergence in diffusion models, providing a rigorous theoretical framework backed by detailed proofs
Rigorous theoretical analysis of class-conditional entropy for Gaussian mixtures with specific, testable predictions (e.g., speciation time scaling)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple models (EDM2-XS, Stable Diffusion 1.5) with consistent findings across different semantic partitions
Practical Algorithm 1 for estimating partitioned entropy from trained models, enabling practical analysis of existing systems
Valuable insights about how guidance redistributes semantic information over time and causes information distortion, with implications for guidance design
Clear and effective visualizations (particularly Figures 1, 4-5) that demonstrate entropy emergence patterns and class-specific signatures
Bridges statistical physics and information theory perspectives, providing new understanding of diffusion model dynamics
Comprehensive appendices with detailed proofs, implementation details, and additional experimental results supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Significant gap between theoretical predictions (sharp phase transitions in clean Gaussian mixtures) and empirical observations (gradual emergence in real data), with explanations that are somewhat post-hoc
Theory relies on idealized Gaussian mixture assumptions that don't hold for real image data, limiting the direct applicability of theoretical insights
Methodological concern: entropy estimation relies on unconditional models as proxies for class posteriors, which introduces bias when the proxy deviates from true class structure
Limited practical prescriptive value - the work is primarily diagnostic, helping understand model behavior rather than improving model design or performance
Modest originality: class-conditional entropy is standard information theory; the novelty lies mainly in applying it to diffusion models rather than developing fundamentally new concepts
Some experimental choices not fully justified or ablated (e.g., Monte Carlo sample sizes, posterior update calibration across noise levels)
The insights about guidance causing information loss are somewhat expected from first principles rather than surprising emergent discoveries
No code released, limiting immediate reproducibility despite sufficient implementation details in appendices
